title: Provide highly effective non-hormonal female contraception without an IUD

concept.text: Provide reversible, self-administered contraception with high pregnancy-prevention efficacy without hormones or an intrauterine procedure. Ovaprene is in phase 3, but its interim pregnancy observations do not establish this higher-efficacy target. Proposed completion test: FDA approval supported by a pivotal typical-use study covering at least 500 woman-years, with a Pearl Index below 2, adequate 13-cycle follow-up, acceptable local safety and prompt return to fertility. Test set by: Proposed editorial efficacy and exposure thresholds; FDA would decide approval. They are not the published Ovaprene performance goal. Sources given: [NICHD female contraceptive development programme](https://annualreport.nichd.nih.gov/blithe.html) ; [Daré regulatory and phase 3 disclosures](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1401914/000140191426000043/dare-20260630.htm) ; [Ovaprene interim trial observations](https://ir.darebioscience.com/news-releases/news-release-details/positive-interim-phase-3-results-highlight-potential-ovaprener-0).

page.title: Nonhormonal female contraception without an IUD
page.definition: A reversible contraceptive that women administer themselves, without hormones or a device placed in the uterus, causes fewer than 1 unintended pregnancy per 100 users in the first year of typical use. Typical use includes incorrect or inconsistent use.

goal.need: FDA's contraceptive guide gives approximately 17 pregnancies per 100 diaphragm users and 21 per 100 internal-condom users over one year, compared with fewer than 1 per 100 copper-IUD users. A self-administered nonhormonal method reaching the latter rate would offer that level of pregnancy prevention without intrauterine placement.

figures.note: FDA's estimates include incorrect or inconsistent use.

statements.quote: These statistics suggest there is a need to develop highly effective non-hormonal contraceptives that have fewer side effects than the currently available methods.
statements.context: The funding announcement discusses contraceptive dissatisfaction, adherence and the limited uptake of intrauterine devices.

statements.quote: Under a CRADA with Dare Bioscience, Ovaprene is being evaluated in the CCTN female method network for contraceptive efficacy, safety and acceptability.
statements.context: CRADA means Cooperative Research and Development Agreement; CCTN means Contraceptive Clinical Trials Network.

statements.quote: There currently are no FDA-approved, hormone-free, monthly intravaginal contraceptives.

completion.title: FDA authorizes a self-administered nonhormonal contraceptive with first-year typical-use failure below 1%.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing authorization for a reversible, self-administered, nonhormonal female contraceptive requiring no intrauterine placement. The accepted clinical evidence establishes fewer than 1 unintended pregnancy per 100 users during the first year of typical use, including incorrect or inconsistent use. Safety and reversibility are supported in the approved evidence package.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback combining NICHD's FDA-approval objective with the HHS Tier 1 contraceptive-effectiveness category.
completion.basis: Searched FDA approval guidance, NICHD development programmes and HHS effectiveness classifications for a combined test covering efficacy, reversibility, self-administration and no hormones or IUD; none was found. This fallback joins NICHD's FDA-approval objective to HHS's Tier 1 typical-use category.

milestones.title: A contraceptive's laboratory and animal evidence supports initial human testing.
milestones.criterion: Nonclinical evidence supports initial human investigation under the applicable drug or device framework. FDA's quoted drug criterion is reasonable safety for initial human testing; device requirements depend on study risk. These are product-specific judgements. For later-stage nonclinical evaluation, Daré's filing for the quarter ended 30 June 2022 reports that Ovaprene was tolerated for several months in sheep. Sample size and detailed toxicology results were not disclosed; this developer report is not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions, for drugs; IDE Approval Process for device investigations. The quoted criterion concerns drugs.
milestones.threshold_quote: Preclinical data to permit an assessment as to whether the product is reasonably safe for initial testing in humans.

milestones.title: A vaginal contraceptive leaves fewer than 5 forward-moving sperm per microscope field after intercourse.
milestones.criterion: In a prespecified postcoital test, midcycle cervical mucus averages fewer than 5 progressively motile sperm per high-power microscope field with the contraceptive, after a baseline cycle averaging at least 5 without it. This is preliminary evidence, not a pregnancy endpoint. In the 2019 Ovaprene study published on 15 January 2024, 38 women enrolled and 23 completed; all 49 evaluable Ovaprene test cycles met the threshold.
milestones.set_by: Ovaprene study investigators, registered study NCT03598088 and its published protocol methods. This test concerns vaginal contraceptives.
milestones.threshold_quote: A test cycle indicative of preliminary contraceptive effectiveness averaged < 5 progressively motile sperm/HPF.

milestones.title: A contraceptive obtains authorization for a pivotal pregnancy-prevention study.
milestones.criterion: The applicable regulator and ethics committees authorize testing in users at risk of pregnancy. For significant-risk devices, FDA IDE and institutional review board approvals are required. Ovaprene's IDE approval was announced on 10 October 2022. Daré's 2026 filing describes at least 2,500 exposure cycles and FDA permission to remove the expectation of 250 participants completing 13 cycles. FDA cautioned that the resulting evidence and the study's Pearl Index performance goal might not support marketing approval.
milestones.set_by: FDA, IDE Approval Process; applied to Ovaprene's pivotal device investigation.
milestones.threshold_quote: both FDA and an Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval prior to initiation of a clinical study.

milestones.title: A pivotal contraceptive study finds fewer than 1 pregnancy per 100 typical users during the first year.
milestones.criterion: A completed pivotal study estimates a first-year typical-use cumulative pregnancy probability below 1%, the published Tier 1 category. Ovaprene's primary endpoint is the 13-cycle Pearl Index, pregnancies per 100 woman-years; 13-cycle cumulative pregnancy probability is secondary. On 12 May 2026, Daré reported a safety review covering 339 participants and 1,789 menstrual cycles, and pregnancy in approximately 9% of treated women. The release gives no pregnancy count or first-year cumulative estimate. These interim results are not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: HHS Office of Population Affairs, Family Planning Annual Report: 2018 National Summary, Appendix C, page C-5. Tier 1 is an effectiveness classification, not Ovaprene's protocol performance goal.
milestones.threshold_quote: less than 1% of women experiencing an unintended pregnancy during the first year of typical use.

not_found: No outside body was found defining the combined completion test for this capability.
No numerical Ovaprene Pearl Index performance goal was found in the opened developer disclosures.
The original FDA letters granting Ovaprene's IDE and approving its 2026 protocol amendment were not located.
ClinicalTrials.gov's accessible pages did not expose the full Ovaprene study records, and its study API could not be opened.
No common early pharmacodynamic threshold covering vaginal and systemic nonhormonal methods was found; the postcoital milestone applies to vaginal products.
The opened Ovaprene nonclinical disclosure did not provide the sheep study's sample size or detailed toxicology results.

results.finding: ZB-06 rat toxicology study, sample size not disclosed: reported no-observed-adverse-effect level was 5 mg/day.
results.detail: The sponsor reported no toxicologically significant adverse effects after nine daily administrations and judged that the animal studies did not raise significant concerns. This is a sponsor protocol, not a reported regulator decision.
results.quote:
Based on the absence of any irritation or any toxicologically significant adverse effects in any 
of the parameters evaluated following daily intravaginal administration of ZB-06 for 9 days to 
adult female rats, the NOAEL for ZB-06 was considered to be 5 mg/day.

results.finding: Ovaprene: 38 women enrolled; all 49 test cycles had fewer than 5 progressively motile sperm per high-power field.
results.detail: Twenty-three participants completed the study. The baseline mean was 27.2 sperm/HPF; both Ovaprene cycle means were 0.5 sperm/HPF. This was a postcoital test, not a pregnancy endpoint.
results.quote: All participants had ≥5 progressively motile sperm/HPF in the baseline cycle and <5 progressively motile sperm/HPF in all 49 Ovaprene cycles and all 35 diaphragm cycles, meeting the definition of a successful postcoital test.

results.finding: ZB-06 vaginal film: 8 participants averaged 0.04 progressively motile sperm per high-power field after intercourse.
results.detail: The no-product baseline averaged 25.9 sperm per field. The test measured a surrogate endpoint, not pregnancy; 20 women enrolled and 8 couples completed all visits.
results.quote: The PCT performed on ovulatory CM at baseline (no product use), revealed a mean of 25.9 (± 30.6) progressively motile sperm (PMS) per high power field (hpf). After use of a single ZB-06 film prior to intercourse, this number dropped to 0.04 (± 0.06) PMS/hpf (p<0.0001).

results.finding: In a phase III trial, 932 women were randomized to C31G; the 12-month pregnancy probability was 13.8%.
results.detail: The modified intent-to-treat estimate included incorrect and inconsistent use and exceeded the 1% threshold. The 12-month extension was optional, and its sample was relatively small.
results.quote: Twelve-month pregnancy probabilities were 13.8% (95%CI 7.6–20%) for C31G and 19.8% (95%CI 10.9–28.7%) for nonoxynol-9.

results.finding: Phexxi phase 3 trial: 1,114 women in the primary effectiveness analysis had a 13.7% seven-cycle typical-use cumulative pregnancy probability.
results.detail: The study reports seven-cycle results, not a first-year estimate. The reported probability exceeds the milestone’s 1% threshold.
results.quote: The seven-cycle cumulative pregnancy percentage was 13.7% [95% confidence interval (CI): 10.0%–17.5%], meeting the prespecified primary endpoint of having the upper bound 95% CI ≤ 21%.
